Called cross-validates three penalties — time-weight decay, unit-weight decay, nuclear-norm penalty L — leaving control cells one time scoring prediction. fitted object exposes per-cell effects, estimated untreated-outcome matrix, selected penalties: Calling autoplot() single trop fit gives synthetic-control-style trajectory: treated-unit average estimated Y(0), dashed line marking first treated period (post-treatment gap two lines effect, left unshaded mistaken confidence band). Fixing penalties hand matches numerically, useful sanity check: lambda_nn = Inf uniform weights low-rank term vanishes fit ordinary two-way fixed effects; finite lambda_nn uniform weights matrix completion; letting cross-validation pick unit time weights gives full TROP estimator. title: TROP implementations compared: the paper, Python, Stata and R
text: Solver. Finite nuclear-norm penalties solved proximal-gradient soft-impute routine, opposed FISTA SCS, implementation depends base R; exact digits therefore need match convex-solver implementations. reconcile difference, fix penalties via lambda = list(time =, unit =, nn =) (bypassing cross-validation), set trop_control(svd = "full"), match implementation’s anchoring. Cross-validation. Penalties chosen leave-one-control-cell-prediction error default (paper’s criterion); placebo criterion resamples actual treatment patterns available via trop_control(cv_method = "placebo"), recommended choice staggered adoption. Per-cell pooled anchoring. anchor = "per_cell" solves separate locally weighted problem treated cell. anchor = "pooled" uses one set weights per treatment spell group – treated cells start end period, pooled across units, group(time) estimands Stata command – faster. block adoption one group; staggered adoption one per cohort; unit switches treatment contributes one group per spell. group’s unit distance average path units periods none treated, comparison unit’s treated cells masked, time weights centred spell midpoint. per-group effects returned fit$tau_groups, ATT cell-weighted average. trop_control(pooled_treat_distance = list(unit = 0, time = 0)) gives group’s units periods full weight (Stata command’s pooled_treat_distance()). trop_matrix() always pooled single trailing block (Python signature). Covariates. Time-varying covariates can supplied trop() panel_compare(); enter low-rank term additively, Section 6.2 paper. Nuclear-norm floor. numerical stability, solver adds small scale-relative floor every finite lambda_nn default (reported lambda_nn include ). lambda_nn = Inf (/TWFE-like case) never affected, trop_control(nn_floor = 0) applies penalties exactly supplied. Standardization. Estimation uses raw outcome default, lambda values outcome’s natural scale; trop(standardize = TRUE) standardizes outcome Stata command , reports lambda standardized scale. Inference. se = "bootstrap" resamples units replacement, keeping unit’s full time series: treated control units separately default (stratified block bootstrap paper Stata command), control units trop_control(boot_resample = "controls") (default Python package’s trop.bootstrap). se = "jackknife" deletes one unit time every unit, Stata command’s vce(jackknife); replicates leave treated unit skipped.
